artists.bio: Third-generation temple mural artist preserving Kerala's Panchavarna natural pigment traditions.
artists.journey: Learned alongside my father in Guruvayur, grinding natural stones and leaves to create the sacred yellow and green ochres.

artists.bio: Master handloom weaver crafting fine Balaramapuram kasavu sarees on pit looms.
artists.journey: Over 40 years behind the pit loom, weaving pure silver and gold zari threads into unbleached handloom cotton.
artists.address: Weavers Colony, Main Road, Balaramapuram, Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala 695501

artists.bio: Lost-wax bronze sculptor and Aranmula metal mirror artisan.
artists.journey: Custodians of the secret bell metal alloy metallurgy passed down through generations in Aranmula village.
artists.address: Heritage Bell Metal Foundry, Temple Road, Aranmula, Kerala 689533

artists.bio: Madhubani painter portraying nature and folklore using bamboo twigs and rice paste.
artists.journey: Painting Kohbar and Bharni styles on handmade lokta paper using soot, turmeric, and indigo extracts.

artists.bio: Terracotta artisan bringing contemporary forms to Malabar clay crafts.
artists.journey: Blending ancient riverbed clay firing techniques with minimalist organic curves.
artists.address: Malabar Clay Craft Guild, Beypore, Kozhikode, Kerala 673015

artworks.title: Ananthasayanam in Panchavarna
artworks.description:
I gathered the yellow stones from the hills behind our temple and prepared the neem tree gum over three weeks. Every eye line is drawn with single squirrel-hair brushes.

Sacred mural depiction using the five pure natural pigments: saffron red, lampblack, ochre yellow, indigo, and kaolin white.
artworks.caption: Living pigments grounded from Kerala soil and stone.

artworks.title: Golden Kasavu Weave with Temple Border
artworks.description:
This border pattern has been in our family ledger since 1952. It requires four pedals and two weavers working in exact harmony to throw the shuttle.

Single-warp pure cotton textile with traditional puliyilakkara (tamarind leaf) border woven with gilded metallic thread.
artworks.caption: Hand-spun elegance on traditional pit looms.

artworks.title: Aranmula Metal Mirror — Vaalkannadi
artworks.description:
Unlike modern glass mirrors where reflection comes from the back coating, this reflects straight from the front polished metallic surface. It took 14 days of constant circular buffing to achieve this clarity.

Front-surface reflection mirror cast from a secretive copper and tin bronze alloy, polished meticulously with velvet and burnt clay.
artworks.caption: A metallurgical miracle with distortion-free optical clarity.

artworks.title: Tree of Life with Sun and Moon
artworks.description:
In our courtyard in Madhubani, women gather during the full moon to paint these intricate blessings for young couples.

Traditional Mithila Kohbar depiction illustrating cosmic vitality, sacred flora, and fish symbols of fertility.
artworks.caption: Hand-painted folklore on handmade rice paper.

artworks.title: Riverbed Terracotta Urn
artworks.description:
The dark charcoal patina is achieved naturally during firing without any chemical glaze. The aroma of wet clay lingers for months.

Smoked unglazed ceramic vessel shaped on an ancestral potter wheel and fired in a wood-and-husk kiln.
artworks.caption: Raw earthy textures of Malabar clay.

artworks.title: Theyyam Spirit of the Forest
artworks.description:
I spent three nights watching the forest shrine rituals in Kannur before picking up the brush. The red represents primal energy and divine justice.

Vibrant portrayal of Pottan Theyyam ritual dance rendered in deep cinnabar red and lamp soot.
artworks.caption: The fiery divine expression of Malabar traditions.

artworks.title: Indigo and Raw Cotton Stole
artworks.description:
Our indigo vat has been alive and fermenting for four seasons. It produces that deep sea blue that only gets richer with every gentle wash.

Natural indigo vat-dyed organic handspun yarn woven with open-sett gossamer borders.
artworks.caption: Fermented plant indigo meets soft rain-fed cotton.

artworks.title: Nataraja Cosmic Dance in Lost-Wax Bronze
artworks.description:
The beeswax model was sculpted entirely by hand, down to the flying locks of hair. Once molten bronze is poured, the wax mold is broken forever.

Classical Chola-style lost-wax bronze casting celebrating the eternal cycle of creation and dissolution.
artworks.caption: Frozen celestial movement in five sacred metals.

artworks.title: Peacocks at Dawn in the Mustard Field
artworks.description:
Every leaf and feather is filled with thousands of micro-strokes. It teaches patience like nothing else in this world.

Double line Bharni painting detailing the joyful plumage of sacred peacocks in spring.
artworks.caption: Intricate cross-hatching done with wild goose quills.

artworks.title: Minimalist Teak Wood Totem
artworks.description:
This timber came from an old dismantled granary in Wayanad. The rings tell stories from before any of us were born.

Hand-carved reclaimed teak sculpture celebrating geometric harmony and natural grain fissures.
artworks.caption: Reclaimed wood sculpted with Japanese hand chisels.

artworks.title: Goddess Saraswati with Veena
artworks.description:
Drawing the curve of the Veena strings requires total breath control. I chant the invocation sloka before beginning the outline.

Mural composition showing the goddess of knowledge sitting on a white lotus with traditional almond-shaped eyes.
artworks.caption: Timeless grace from the sanctum walls.

artworks.title: Handwoven Khadi Shawl with Madder Red Border
artworks.description:
The warmth of khadi is incomparable. It breathes in the humid Kerala monsoons and insulates in the evening sea breeze.

Lightweight breathable shawl spun on traditional Ambar charkha and border dyed with natural madder root.
artworks.caption: The tactile rhythm of handspun khadi.

artworks.title: Traditional Brass Nilavilakku Lamp
artworks.description:
When fueled with cold-pressed sesame oil and cotton wicks, the light illuminates the room with a warm golden resonance.

Nine-tiered temple oil lamp hand-lathed and engraved with floral motifs and the sacred Hamsa bird crest.
artworks.caption: Lighting prayer spaces for centuries.

artworks.title: Ganga Arati Ceremonial Boat
artworks.description:
I painted this after a pilgrimage to Haridwar. The small lights in the dark water felt like stars that fell into the river.

Narrative folk painting capturing earthen diyas floating on sacred river waters under dusk skies.
artworks.caption: A tribute to eternal river folklore.

artworks.title: Smoke-Fired Clay Water Carafe
artworks.description:
Water stored in this pitcher tastes sweet and grounding. The surface is polished with smooth river pebbles before firing.

Ergonomic pitcher keeping drinking water naturally chilled using porous clay evaporation.
artworks.caption: Ancient cooling wisdom in contemporary clay design.

artworks.title: Forest Elephant with Golden Howdah
artworks.description:
The golden nettipattam on the elephant's forehead took four days of fine gold leaf and yellow ochre stippling.

Celebrated temple festival iconography featuring the majestic caparisoned tusker against monsoon clouds.
artworks.caption: The soul of Kerala's temple pageantry.

artworks.title: Kasavu Tussar Silk Saree with Geometric Pallu
artworks.description:
The natural gold sheen of tussar silk needs no bleaching. It honors the wilderness where the silkworms feed on Asan trees.

Textured raw tussar silk blended with traditional gold zari patterns in the pallu.
artworks.caption: Wild tussar cocoons spun into regal evening attire.

artworks.title: Bronze Temple Bell with Nandi Finial
artworks.description:
The alloy proportions determine how long the bell rings. When struck gently, the chime lingers in the air for over 25 seconds.

High-acoustic resonance bell producing sustained 432 Hz overtone vibrations.
artworks.caption: Acoustic perfection cast in sacred bell metal.

artworks.title: Fish of Life in Sacred Lotus Pond
artworks.description:
In our lore, the twin fish protect homes from misfortune. I used fresh pomegranate skin boiled with alum for the warm ochre tones.

Interlocking geometric fish and lotus petals symbolising prosperity and calm waters.
artworks.caption: Ancient symbols of auspicious fortune.

artworks.title: Architectural Ceramic Wall Relief
artworks.description:
I wanted to prove that traditional village clay craft can hold its own on the walls of modern architectural spaces worldwide.

Modular terracotta tiles featuring abstract river contours for gallery interiors.
artworks.caption: Earth and heat forged into architectural form.
